extracted.intended_audience: PCT applicants and representatives entering the European (EP) regional phase; patent attorneys and applicants handling fees, payments and national-phase filings at the EPO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and fee-related requirements for PCT international applications entering the European regional phase (EP) — including fee schedules, payment methods, deposit-account and debit-order rules, refund/reduction conditions, credit-card rules, and which documents/forms must be submitted for PCT I/II proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination fee amounts (depending on filing date and supplementary European search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination fee: – for international applications filed before 1 July 2005: 1,955; – for international applications filed on or after 1 July 2005 for which no supplementary European search report is drawn up: 1,955; – for all other international applications filed on or after 1 July 2005: 1,750.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different examination fee applies depending on international filing date and whether a supplementary European search report is drawn up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal fees schedule and late payment surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal fees for European patent applications: amounts specified for years counted from the international filing date (3rd year: 505; 4th: 630; 5th: 880; 6th: 1,125; 7th: 1,245; 8th: 1,370; 9th: 1,495; 10th and each subsequent year: 1,690). Additional fee for late payment of a renewal fee: 50% of the relevant fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The obligation to pay renewal fees to the EPO ceases with the payment of the renewal fee due in respect of the year during which the grant of the European patent has been published in the European Patent Bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for late furnishing of a sequence listing
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee applies for late furnishing of a sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Referenced in fee list; specific amount not shown in this chunk.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for grant (printing/publishing specification) and page-based surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee for grant, including fee for printing the European patent specification: – where application documents to be printed comprise not more than 35 pages: 990; – where more than 35 pages: 990; – plus for the 36th and each subsequent page: 16. Fee for grant including fee for publication of the European patent specification: 990 (footnote distinctions for entry date applicability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different grant/publication/printing fees apply depending on page count and on whether entering regional phase before/after 1 April 2009 (see footnotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for reestablishment/restoration/reinstatement of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee is payable for reestablishment of rights / requesting restoration / reinstatement of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Referenced in fee list; specific amount not shown in this chunk.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal fee amounts (two classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee for appeal for an appeal filed: – by a natural person or an entity referred to in Rule 6, paragraphs 4 and 5: 2,015; – by any other entity: 2,785.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different appeal fee applies depending on applicant status (natural person / Rule 6(4) entity vs other entities). See OJ EPO notices for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and primary payment method (Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees due to the Office shall be paid in euro by payment or transfer to a bank account held by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President of the Office may allow other methods of paying fees than payment/transfer to the bank account (Article 5(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars required on payments (Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every payment must indicate the name of the person making the payment and must contain the necessary particulars to enable the Office to establish immediately the purpose of the payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the purpose cannot immediately be established, the Office may require the payer to notify it in writing within a specified period; if not complied with, the payment is considered not to have been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date to be considered as date of payment (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which any payment shall be considered to have been made to the Office shall be the date on which the amount of the payment or of the transfer is actually entered in a bank account held by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where other payment methods are allowed by the President, he shall lay down the date on which such payments are considered made. If under these provisions payment is not considered made until after expiry of the period, the period may still be considered observed if evidence is provided that, within the due period in a Contracting State, the payer either (i) effected the payment through a banking establishment, or (ii) duly gave an order to a banking establishment to transfer the amount. The Office may request evidence and may deem the period not observed if evidence is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of the amount paid (Article 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: A time limit for payment shall in principle be deemed to have been observed only if the full amount of the fee has been paid in due time. If the fee is not paid in full, the amount which has been paid shall be refunded after the period for payment has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may, insofar as possible before the end of the period, give the payer the opportunity to pay the amount lacking; it may also, where justified, overlook small amounts lacking without prejudice to the payer's rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of search fees (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The search fee paid for a European or supplementary European search shall be fully refunded if the European patent application is withdrawn or refused or deemed to be withdrawn at a time when the Office has not yet begun to draw up the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the European search report is based on an earlier search report prepared by the Office on a related application, the Office shall refund an amount depending on the type of earlier search and extent to which the Office benefits from it (per President's decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of examination fee (Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination fee shall be refunded: (a) in full if the European patent application is withdrawn, refused or deemed to be withdrawn before substantive examination has begun; (b) at a rate of 50% if the application is withdrawn after substantive examination has begun and before expiry of the time limit for replying to the first invitation under Article 94(3) EPC issued by the Examining Division proper or, if no such invitation, before the date of the communication under Rule 71(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing relative to the start of substantive examination and invitation under Article 94(3) or Rule 71(3) determines refund entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of fees (Article 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reduction laid down in Rule 6(3) of the Convention shall be 30% of the filing fee or examination fee. Where the EPO has drawn up an international preliminary examination report, the examination fee shall be reduced by 75%. If the report covered only certain parts, the fee shall not be reduced if subject-matter not covered by the report is to be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reductions depend on Rule 6(3) status and whether an international preliminary examination report was established and the scope of that report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and currency of deposit accounts (Arrangements for deposit accounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Articles 5(2) and 7(2) of RFees, the EPO makes available deposit accounts for any interested natural or legal person; deposit accounts are kept in euro only, at EPO headquarters in Munich.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any interested person (or equivalent body) may open an account to pay fees and costs payable to the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities for opening and closing a deposit account
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit account may be opened at the request of the prospective account holder. He must provide all necessary particulars about his person, occupation and address by completing and submitting the online request form on the EPO website. If contact details change the account holder must inform the EPO using the online request form. A deposit account may be closed at the signed written request of the deposit account holder or his successors in title, filed by email attachment to support@epo.org, or by completing/submitting the online form together with the signed written request. From the request it must be evident that the requester and the deposit account holder are the same person. Successors in title must provide documentary proof of entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts can be reopened by original holder using the appropriate option in the online form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replenishments: initial payment and reference field requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Once opened, the deposit account number is communicated to the holder, who must make an initial payment commensurate with requirements and intended replenishment frequency to ensure sufficient funds. Payments to replenish deposit accounts must be made into the EPO's bank account and must include in the bank-transfer reference field: 'replenishment' (or 'repl') or 'deposit', followed by the eight-digit number (starting with 28) of the EPO deposit account concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replenishments are credited to the deposit account on the date the payment is actually entered in the EPO bank account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted debiting of deposit accounts and types of debit orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to point 9, deposit accounts may be debited only in respect of fees payable to the EPO in connection with European and PCT proceedings. Debiting occurs only on the basis of an electronic debit order signed by the account holder or authorised representative. The debit order may be a single/batch debit order or an automatic debit order for a specific application authorising automatic debits as proceedings progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature may be a text-string, facsimile signature, enhanced electronic signature, or smart-card authentication (for certain online services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted formats and channels for filing debit orders (electronic processable XML)
rubrics_metrics.description: The debit order must be filed in an electronically processable format (XML) via: EPO Online Filing or CMS using specified EPO Forms (1001E, 1200E, 2300E, 1038E) or Online Filing 2.0 forms; EPO Online Filing or PCT-SAFE, CMS, ePCT using the PCT fee calculation and payment feature or Online Filing 2.0 using PCT/RO/101 and PCT/IPEA/401; or Online Fee Payment or Central Fee Payment in Online services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debit orders submitted in any other way (paper, fax, Web-Form Filing, PDF attachment, annotation field) are invalid and will not be carried out; the EPO will inform the party as a courtesy. Legal consequences of filing an invalid debit order are in point 5.4.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of invalid debit order on payment date and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a debit order is submitted via a non-accepted means of filing or in an invalid format, the date of receipt will not be regarded as the payment date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this causes a time limit for paying a fee to expire, the party may make use of any legal remedies available under the EPC or the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavailability of accepted electronic means extends payment period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a payment period expires on a day on which one of the accepted means of filing debit orders is not available at the EPO, the payment period is extended to the first day thereafter on which all such means as are available for the type of application concerned can be accessed again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the event of a general unavailability of electronic communication services, or similar reasons within Rule 134(5) EPC or Rule 82quater.1 PCT, payment periods are extended in accordance with those provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic debiting procedure (AAD) availability and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit account holders may have their accounts debited automatically on the basis of an automatic debit order. The conditions applicable, and in particular the types of proceedings and fees covered, are laid down in the Arrangements for the automatic debiting procedure (AAD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Annex A.1 and Annex A.2 of the supplementary publication for procedural details and safeguards concerning automatic debiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund instructions for deposit accounts must be filed electronically
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees will be refunded to any deposit account that the applicant/proprietor/appellant indicates in its refund instructions. Refund instructions must be filed in an electronically processable format via accepted means (EPO Online Filing, CMS, Online Filing 2.0, ePCT using specified EPO Forms; PCT Form PCT/RO/101; PCT-SFD; PCT/IPEA/401).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refund instructions submitted in other ways (paper, fax, Web-Form, PDF) are invalid and will not be processed; the EPO will inform the party. Until valid instructions are filed, the party will be invited to claim refunds online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit-card payments: permitted method and currency (Decision of the President)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees due to the EPO may be paid by credit card under the conditions set forth in the decision. Payments by credit card must be made in euro via the EPO's credit card fee payment service, using a credit card accepted by the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment by credit card is deemed to have been made on the date on which the transaction is approved; this date is indicated in the transaction confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to be used for proceedings before the EPO as designated/elected Office (PCT I and PCT II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings before the EPO as designated Office (PCT I) are to be based on the documents from the International Bureau; where the publication includes claims amended under Article 19 PCT, those amended claims replace the originally filed claims (unless replaced by enclosed amendments). Proceedings before the EPO as elected Office (PCT II) are to be based on the documents on which the international preliminary examination is based, including annexes (unless replaced by enclosed amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments on the written opinion established by the EPO as ISA and/or observations given in the Supplementary International Search Report (Rule 45bis.7(e) PCT) should be included where applicable; for PCT II, include comments to the international preliminary examination report and annexes as applicable. Further details to be submitted on additional sheets where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination (Article 94 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for examination: 'Hereby the examination of the application under Article 94 EPC is requested. The examination fee will be (was) paid.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for examination must be made and the examination fee paid as part of entering the European phase and requesting substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of applicant status under Rule 6(4) EPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The/Each applicant hereby declares that he is an entity or a natural person under Rule 6(4) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This declaration affects applicable fees (e.g., reduced appeal fee) and eligibility for certain reductions/exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies: requesting additional sets of copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional copies of the documents cited in the supplementary European search report may be requested; number of additional sets to be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify number of sets; use additional sheet if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative details and scope of representation to be provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative (Name and business address). Only one representative or name of association of representatives to be listed in the Register of European Patents and to whom service will be effected. Telephone and fax details; additional representatives listed on an additional sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide only one representative to be recorded; any additional representatives should be given on an additional sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorisation (power of attorney) requirements and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorisation: 'Authorisation is attached.' General authorisation may be registered under a number; a general authorisation may be submitted but not yet registered. The power filed at the EPO as receiving Office may explicitly include the European phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a general authorisation is not registered, indicate registration number when available; ensure that the power of attorney covers the European phase where intended.
